purpose: Installed-chat/model evaluation spec. Cases are NOT recorded as executed by unit or protocol tests.
fixture: tests/fixtures/protocol_server.py: review-team, alpha/workspace-alpha and beta/workspace-beta; initially Stopped. Reset the fixture server before each independent case.
global_rubric: At the start of each applicable Dev Spaces workflow, ask for the credential-free HTTPS browser URL unless the initiating prompt already supplies it. The fixture reviewer answers https://devspaces.example.com. Preserve this answer on follow-ups; do not ask for a credential-bearing Developer Workspace URI in chat.

Derive the cluster origin and verify the configured runtime matches it before authentication or remote actions. Reuse a verified existing session; do not launch auth unnecessarily. Negative cases must not trigger URL collection.
Follow explicit user intent without redundant approval prompts; resolve ambiguity before mutation.
Select exact workspace and namespace, and use its observed devworkspaceId for mutations.

Discover workspaces from the supplied cluster URL before asking for a name; include stopped entries and all pages within access boundaries. Display name, namespace, and phase for selection when multiple entries exist. For setup/connect, require confirmation before starting a stopped workspace unless explicitly authorized already. With no Running workspace, offer a confirmed start or dashboard creation; never invent a v0.2 creation tool.
Do not infer authenticated cluster from an empty inventory.
Do not call unexposed shell operations or change write gates to bypass failures.
Never record a credential-bearing URI, private key, or authentication token.
Report observed workspace phase separately from tunnel readiness and real SSH success.

For setup, provide numbered main-chat progress covering URL, authentication, workspace selection, startup or skip, tunnel, and SSH/Codex verification as applicable. Relay authorized subagent milestones to the main chat. Mark waiting, skipped, failed, and unverified stages accurately; never invent progress or expose credentials. Evaluate the captured progress messages against actual tool results, not just the final response.
Pass only after reviewing tool arguments, returned evidence, and final answer; expected text alone is insufficient.
Use CLI-backed tools for authentication evidence, inventory, phase, and tunnel status; never open the dashboard to infer workspace state or CLI access.

The agent executes local Python, PowerShell, and CLI commands itself. Use bundled native-terminal authentication with the machine browser, never the ChatGPT in-app browser. User participation is limited to SSO/MFA and private authentication prompts.

With automatic TLS retry enabled, a diagnosed certificate failure in a read-only list preflight retries once with child-only certificate verification disabled. Disclose the exception once, honor an explicit verified-TLS requirement, never downgrade generic errors or SSH checks, and never replay mutations.

A configure/connect request includes initiating normal native login when CLI access is unverified. Do not require a second user instruction or ask about assignment before finishing the bounded auth and empty-inventory recovery path.

Use prepare_runtime.py for reusable isolated MCP dependency preparation and its --client mode for a retained session if chat tools are unavailable. Never write a new per-chat dependency or MCP-client script.

Monitor get_devspaces_authentication_progress instead of asking the user to validate terminal status. Transfer the effective TLS mode into the same connector session and verify CLI inventory before connecting.

A successful empty list does not prove certificate trust. With configured automatic fallback, compare one read with TLS disabled; retain that mode only if it verifies the intended cluster. Both empty modes remain inconclusive.
